section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the three meanings of "One" in the Shema, the distinction between idolatry and partnership, and the nature of Divine providence over all creatures.
section.t: And to understand all this, one must understand
the statement of our Rabbis, of blessed memory, in Berachot
a)
"You have made Me a single entity in the world, and I will make you a single entity in the world."
"You have made Me a single entity—'Hear O Israel, the L-rd our G-d, the L-rd is One'—and I will make you a single entity,
'And who is like Your people Israel, a unique nation on earth,' for in both it is stated 'One': 'the L-rd is One' and 'a unique nation.'
Now, regarding "one," there are three matters:
In the Midrash it is said: "One—there is none like Him."
And one must understand what the praise of "there is none like Him" is, for how could it enter a person's mind that there is something like Him, that we need to say there is none like Him?
And the second matter in "the L-rd is One" is that which is stated in the Midrash Rabbah:
"From where did Israel merit the Shema? From the Giving of the Torah.
The Holy One, blessed be He, said: 'Hear O Israel, I am the L-rd your G-d.' Israel answered: 'The L-rd is our G-d.'
'You shall have no other gods...' Israel answered: 'The L-rd is One.'
And this means that He is One, to exclude the matter of idolatry."
And the third is that "the L-rd is One" is a commandment in itself,
which is the commandment to unify Him, and this is from the verse "Hear O Israel, the L-rd our G-d, the L-rd is One,"
and this is to exclude the matter of partnership.
For behold, the descendants of Noah are not commanded regarding partnership, according to the opinion of the Rema in Orach Chaim, section 156.
Although they are commanded regarding idolatry, for Adam the First was commanded about this, as it is written "And He commanded..." and "command"
refers only to idolatry, etc.,
nevertheless, regarding partnership they were not commanded,
and only Israel was commanded regarding partnership.
And the difference between idolatry and partnership is:
Idolatry is that which they call
"the G-d of gods."
For behold, "High above
all nations is the L-rd; above the heavens is His glory"—they say
that He is high and exalted, and therefore His glory is only above the heavens,
but regarding the lower and lowly creations, it is a degradation for Him to supervise them, and "the L-rd has forsaken the earth" to the hands of the stars and constellations of the heavens.
And this is according to their reasoning that the creation of the world
is in the manner of cause and effect, which is in the aspect of proportion, etc., as is known,
and therefore they say that the heavens, i.e., the upper creations, are worthy for Him to supervise them,
but the lower effects are not worthy of His supervision, only "He has forsaken the earth and all that is in it" to the hands of the stars and constellations of the heavens.
But in truth it is not so, for "He who dwells on high, humbles Himself to behold the heavens and the earth"—
because He dwells on high, in the aspect of separation, therefore He humbles Himself regarding the heavens and the earth equally,
for even the heavens are a degradation relative to Him,
because creation is not in the manner of cause and effect,

for in the manner of cause and effect, it would be impossible for even the most elevated levels to exist, for even the existence of light is specifically through the contraction that occurred in the Ein Sof,
for the light that is included in His Essence is not in the category of light at all, as stated in the Zohar: "They are not lights," etc., and as stated in Sefer Shemuel
with the analogy of the light and radiance of the sun within the sun, which is not called by the name "light" and "radiance" at all, etc.
Therefore, the revelation of the line

from the Ein Sof is called "yesh me'ayin" (something from nothing), because in its source in the Ein Sof, blessed be He, it is in the aspect of nothingness, etc., as stated in Likkutei Torah, in the discourse beginning "Tiku," in the gloss.
And all the more so the creation of the vessels and the worlds, which are in a manner of incomparability,

and therefore Adam Kadmon is called the "man of the creation of the totality," because there is there the aspect of vessels, which is the aspect of creation, in the aspect of the renewal of something, etc., as stated elsewhere.
And the Ramak, of blessed memory, in the book "Elimah,"
wrote that more than the incomparability of Asiyah relative to Keter, is the incomparability of Keter relative to the Ein Sof.
(And see what is stated in the Pardes, in the Gate of Tztachtzachot, that Keter is the root of the vessels,

for from the Ein Sof the aspects of lights were emanated, and from Keter, which bears the Ein Sof and is concealed within it, the vessels were emanated, etc., and this is as stated in the Tikunei Zohar:
"The Ein Sof is within, Keter is the supernal crown without," etc.).
And it is found that even the most elevated levels are an aspect of degradation relative to Him.

And just as "above the heavens is His glory," so too is His providence upon the earth, over the creations, for He supervises every single detail, as stated in the Gemara, Chullin 63a: "When he saw a cormorant, he said, 'Your judgments are like the great deep,' and when he saw an ant, he said, 'Your righteousness is like the mighty mountains.'" And Rashi explains: "An ant has vitality like a large creature,
and 'Your judgments' are even in the great deep, for You have prepared the cormorant to judge and execute Your vengeance upon the fish of the sea, to kill those destined to die."
And from this, our master, the Baal Shem Tov, brought a response to those who say that Divine providence is only over the human species,
for behold, among the fish of the sea there is judgment and justice, and He prepares the cormorant to judge and execute His vengeance upon those destined, etc. And in the Midrash:
"And He sent"—even a bird is not caught without Heaven, for a heavenly voice goes forth and proclaims 'Demos' or 'Sekula,' etc.
And what our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said
in Avodah Zarah 4a, on the verse "And You make man like the fish of the sea"—just as fish in the sea, every larger one swallows its fellow, etc., so too among human beings, etc.,
this is not without judgment and justice, for it is all with providence and with judgment and justice,
and the proof is that we learn from this that it is also so with man, and regarding man, everyone agrees that there is individual providence.

And this is why "Pray for the welfare of the government, for were it not for the fear of it, a man would swallow his fellow alive"—this is with providence, and nevertheless, "pray for its welfare," etc., for such is the supernal conduct,
and it is found from all this that there is individual providence over the creations, over every single detail of theirs.

And those who worship the sun, the moon, and all the host of heaven, which I did not command, and do not believe, etc., and remove His providence entirely from the earth and all that is in it, and say "The L-rd has forsaken," etc.—this is idolatry, regarding which Adam the First was commanded, "And He commanded," etc.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the concept of partnership, distinguishing it from idolatry, and how Israel's unique relationship with G-d prohibits attributing any independent power to natural forces.
section.t: However, the matter of partnership is a different matter.
For behold, our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said:
"There are three partners in a person: father, mother, and the Holy One, blessed be He, who gives him a soul."
And behold, the main part is the portion of the Holy One, blessed be He,

for when the soul departs from the body, the portion of father and mother remains like a silent stone, for the vessel of intellect does not think, the eye does not see, the ear does not hear, etc., everything is nullified,
and also in the portion of father and mother themselves, the main thing is the Divine power, as stated by our Rabbis, of blessed memory:
"There is no rock like our G-d, there is no artist like our G-d, who forms a form within a form."
And the entirety of the matter of birth is through the power of the Ein Sof, as it is written: "Male and female He created them... and He blessed them," etc.
And just as we see empirically that there are several people for whom, from a natural perspective, there is no impediment to birth, yet they do not give birth,
this is because birth is through the power of the Ein Sof.
Nevertheless, father and mother are called "partners," and this is the commandment in the Ten Commandments to honor them, as it is written: "Honor your father and your mother," etc.
And this is because they possess free will, as Ben Azzai said:
"What can I do, for my soul yearns for Torah?"
Behold, the cause of his existence is nevertheless dependent on father and mother, who have free will in this,
therefore they are called "partners."
And if so, it is understood from this that regarding that which does not have free choice and acts in a compelled manner, one cannot ascribe to it the matter of partnership.
And like the earth, from which bread comes forth,
for when one sows wheat in the earth and rains fall, it sprouts through the vegetative power in the earth,
behold, the earth does not have free will in this, that the wheat should not sprout,
for from the vegetative power in the earth, which is the Divine utterance "Let the earth sprout forth," it automatically sprouts when one sows in it,
and similarly, what is written:
"With the precious things of the sun's produce and the precious things of the moon's yield"—behold, this is not in the choice of the sun and moon, as it is written:
"He who commands the sun, and it does not shine"—that it is not in the choice of the sun not to radiate light, or that the light should not be hot,
and similarly regarding the light of the moon, that it should not be cold,
and therefore, although the influence comes through them, one cannot ascribe to them the matter of partnership, for they are like an axe in the hand of the hewer,
and just as an axe that hews stones from the mountain, one cannot ascribe to it partnership in the craft, for it has nothing in this except that the person hews through it,
so too the sun, moon, and all the host of heaven, since they have no free will at all, they are only like an axe, etc., and one cannot ascribe to them the matter of partnership.
However, regarding this, only Israel was commanded, as it is written: "Hear O Israel, the L-rd our G-d, the L-rd is One,"
and the descendants of Noah are not commanded regarding this,
for "He set the boundaries
of the peoples according to the number of the children of Israel"—seventy souls, the descendants of Yaakov,
and this means that the reception of their influence is through the seventy princes,
and only the souls of Israel, regarding which it is written: "The L-rd's portion is His people,"

they were commanded regarding partnership, not to associate the Divine Name with anything, as it is written: "And you shall know this day... that the L-rd is G-d... there is none else"—that there is nothing besides Him at all,
and as it is written: "See
now that I, I am He, and there is no god with Me"—there is no partner with Me.

And the outcome of this, in the negation of partnership, is that regarding father and mother, who are partners because of their free will as above, one must honor them, since they are nevertheless a cause for his existence,
but the negation of partnership from the stars and constellations, which have no free will in the influence and have no partnership at all in this,

consequently, one should not honor them nor consider them, and similarly, one should not consider the physical things with which he occupies himself, since they are not the cause of his influence, for it is Divinity that influences him, and "He is the One who gives you strength to make wealth,"
and the physical thing is only a vessel through which the influence passes, like an axe in the hand of the hewer.
If so, the vessel must be in the ultimate state of fitness,
that it be worthy of G-d's blessing,
and one should not be sunken and troubled in it,
and he should not bow his head—meaning his intellect—to it, and there should be no confusion or any hindrance or impediment to Torah and prayer,

and on the contrary, his main focus should be on Divine matters, and in the physical things themselves, there should be a Divine intention, that he can perform a mitzvah and guide his children in the way of the L-rd,
and through this, he draws down the revelation of "the L-rd is One," meaning that there will be a revelation of Divinity in the world.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section distinguishes between the revelations of Gan Eden and the World to Come, explaining that the latter is achieved through the refinement of physical matter in this world.
section.t: And the matter is that in the Zohar, it is asked:
"What is 'See now'? And behold, 'I, I am He' refers to the future, so what is 'See now'?"
And one must first explain what is the matter of the two times "I,"
for behold, now it is stated once "I," like "I am the L-rd,"
and what is the matter that regarding the future, two times "I" are stated?
And the implication is that there will be a unification of the two times "I," which is the matter of "I, I am He."
And behold, the two times "I" are "I am the first and I am the last," and one must explain what is the matter that in the future there will be two times "I" in unification.
And one must briefly explain the root of the difference
between Gan Eden and the World to Come, i.e., the World of Resurrection,
for Gan Eden is the pleasure of souls without bodies,
and there are different levels in Gan Eden,
the Upper Gan Eden and the Lower Gan Eden,
although there are many levels in Gan Eden, and as above, "Torah scholars have no rest, neither in this world nor in the World to Come, as it is said: 'They go from strength to strength,'"
nevertheless, in general, they are two levels that are distinct from each other, in the manner of the hidden world and the revealed world,
and in each there are several levels,
and there are souls whose all ascents are in the Lower Gan Eden and they do not merit the Upper Gan Eden, for it is a level unto itself.
And the World to Come is one level, and as the statement: "All of Israel have a portion in the World to Come,"
although each one is singed by the canopy
of his fellow, nevertheless, in general, it is one level, unlike Gan Eden, which is two levels as above,
and the World to Come will be for souls specifically in bodies.
And one must explain why souls that have been in Gan Eden for more than three thousand years, like the Patriarchs and Moshe,
will need to clothe themselves in bodies—why was this so before Him, blessed be He, that they should return and clothe themselves in bodies?
And what is the preciousness of the pleasure that it is worthwhile for this to clothe oneself in a body?
However, the matter is that Gan Eden is the pleasure of souls in the study of the laws in spirituality,

for those laws that below are "Two are holding a tallit" and "One who exchanges a cow for a donkey," they study there in spirituality and comprehend the essence of the thing, and this is that they enjoy the radiance of the Shechinah, as stated elsewhere.

And this is a wondrous pleasure without end, and the revelation of Gan Eden is through the study of Torah below, for through those below who engage in Torah, through this they merit the study and comprehension of Torah in Gan Eden, and as the statement:
"Fortunate is he who comes here with his learning in his hand"—the learning he learned in this world, through this is the revelation of Gan Eden.
However, the revelation of the future is through the clarifications below,
and this means not only from the occupation with Torah, but from the clarifications that one clarifies through the power of Torah,
and similarly in mitzvot, from the performance of mitzvot with physical things, which are clarified through this.
And therefore it is called "a day that is entirely Shabbat," for the revelation of Shabbat is through the preparation of the six weekdays, for "one who toils

on Erev Shabbat will eat on Shabbat," and this is through the work of clarifications during the six days of the week, as it is written: "Six days shall you work," etc., and like the revelation of the future, "a day that is entirely Shabbat," is after the completion of the clarifications of the six thousand years, etc.
